name: Plan Transitions
description: Plans transitions between A-roll and B-roll clips based on creative direction.

inputs.name: cut_decisions
inputs.description: Step 3.03's narrative verdict per cut - smooth | acceptable | jarring | broken, with the review's own sentence. Routed to this step's BRIDGE, which folds it onto `cuts_toon` as `narrative_verdict` and `verdict_note` keyed on `cut_point_position`, the identifier both tables already share. Deliberately NOT in `context_fields`: sending the raw list beside the table would ship the same judgement twice (AGENTS.md 10.1). Optional, because a review that judged no cut is a review that had nothing to say - an unjudged cut reads as `unjudged`, never as `smooth`. See library/tools/cut_verdicts.py.

inputs.name: semantic_analysis
inputs.description: Semantic analysis output. Read by bridge.py only - joined to the catalog and summarised into the two footage columns of cuts_toon, never sent raw to the prompt.

inputs.name: clip_catalog
inputs.description: State input: clip_catalog. Read by bridge.py only - it is what joins a semantic document (keyed by file stem) to the clip_id the spine speaks.

inputs.name: creative_brief
inputs.description: The captain's creative direction as markdown, injected by the runner from the project's creative_brief path. Empty when the project declares none.

inputs.name: project_context
inputs.description: The project's context folder plus the learnings routed to this step, as a MAP the model follows with its shell (never a copy). Injected by the runner from the project's context/ folder and learned_context/ store when this step declares it; a stated absence when the project has neither. See library/tools/project_context.py.

inputs.name: timeline_notes
inputs.description: The captain's own notes typed onto the built timeline in DaVinci Resolve, routed to this step because this step owns the decision each note is about. Injected by the runner from <project>/marker_feedback/ and absent when there are none. See library/tools/marker_routing.py.

inputs.name: project_fps
inputs.description: Timebase from the catalog. `duration_frames` is computed from it, and until this edge existed the post-bridge read `frame_rate` - a key nothing in the pipeline produces - and every transition on a 23.976 fps project was cut at 30.0. Same declaration, same reason, as step 4.04's.

inputs.name: prosody_analysis
inputs.description: State input: prosody_analysis. Read through view:emphasis only - the per-block most-emphasized words a cut may anchor to. Optional because a run that measured no prosody still cuts; the view states the absence in one line.

outputs.name: cuts_toon
outputs.description: State output: cuts_toon. Built by bridge.py. Carries can_carry_drawn_transition / carry_basis, derived from library/tools/transition_carriers.py - which cuts have a V1 clip ending on them and can therefore carry a drawn transition.

outputs.name: cuts_unjudged
outputs.description: Bridge output: how much of the rough-cut review's judgement is missing, said rather than left to be inferred from a column of `unjudged` (library/tools/cut_verdicts.unjudged_summary). Emitted only on runs where any cut went unjudged; when every cut was judged the absence means nothing is missing, not a value to invent (AGENTS.md 10.5). Declared here because the bridge emits it on such runs and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

llm_outputs.name: transition_creative
llm_outputs.description: One entry per cut, each at a DISTINCT cut_point_position (the spine position of the INCOMING block). Fields: cut_point_position, type, duration_feel, rationale, plus OPTIONAL anchor (the exact point of the cut: {word} in the OUTGOING block, {beat}/{bar+beat}/{downbeat} on the measured grid, {motion_peak}/{action_onset} on the outgoing block's measured action, or {frame}; with optional offset_seconds/offset_frames; no anchor_end on a cut). A boundary may ALSO carry one J/L audio-offset entry (type j_cut with lead_seconds, or l_cut with lag_seconds, and/or an anchor resolving in the outgoing (J) or incoming (L) block; no duration_feel, fallback_type or anchor_end on it): the picture stays the resolved cut and the audio edit point moves by the offset, with the opened gap filled by measured room tone. An anchored cut lands exactly where the anchor resolves, winning over the word-end and beat-snap; an unresolvable anchor refuses the step. Empty is a legitimate answer on a cut-less edit - and where no cut earned a drawn gesture; the post-bridge carries no floor and adds none.
